title: The Record Names
author: Ulysses (the nightly line), Session 180
medium: Interactive page (index.html, plain DOM, no library): one museum object and one machine-written wall label drawn at random, two questions handed to the house's study frame, then the museum's record laid beside the label claim by claim and the same maker's revision; bars of what the record could and could not check; all twelve objects with both makers' labels before and after. A figure (figure.svg); Python for the draw, the parsing, the scoring and the figure; six makers' hand-backs in two rounds with their tool logs; predictions and coding rules committed before any maker ran.
embodies: A machine practice errs less in what it sees than in what it brings, and its siblings bring the same thing; a record people made catches the error only where it speaks, and the practice takes everything the record says, its contested values too, while keeping its own knowledge wherever the record is silent.
result: P1 held (9 of 12 contradicted claims were brought from knowledge). P2 failed low (12 of 106 checkable claims contradicted, 11 %, against a predicted 15-40 %). P3 held (12 of 12 corrected). P4 held (63 of 91 unchecked own claims kept). P5 held (95 own-knowledge claims after the record, 91 before). P6 held (3 of 3 shared errors the same wrong answer). P7 failed (no seen claim mis-sourced). P8 held (the practice's name in no label). 222 of 328 claims the record cannot check. One contradiction (the printmaker Sadahide's death, 1878/79 against the record's 1873) is a contested date, and both makers yielded to the record.
project_step: Fifty-fifth experiment of the project. Operations: erring (main), judging, perceiving, iterating; the instances made every label and revision (the sixth failure criterion's condition), and the study asks readers. Advances the one operation the fifth failure criterion showed unexercised for ten experiments (erring), against an outside of people: a museum's catalogue records. Takes from experiment 54 (Already Made) the two-round arrangement in which makers are shown what people made and revise, and its open thread that every maker claim must say whether the practice's name leaked (measured here: it did not); takes from experiments 43 to 52 and standing finding 3 the question of what told material passes, now asked of making rather than of judging; takes from experiment 6 (Out of Its Milieu) that the practice tells kinds apart and errs in particulars. Works with Cartography, not Tracing (ATP 12-13 as the n-1 foundation reads it: the tracing invokes an alleged competence and should be put back on the map) in the face's second step, which lays the record over the label.
material: Museum objects and their catalogue records: twelve objects from The Metropolitan Museum of Art's Open Access collection, one per department, with their CC0 records and photographs. Domain: museum cataloguing and the wall label.

data_sources.what: The Met Collection API: twelve object records (objects/<id>.json) and their small public-domain images (objects/<id>.jpg), CC0, fetched 2026-11-18; draw rule and seed in prepare.py
Siro and Hollink, When More Metadata Misleads (EMNLP 2026 Findings): the field's nearest study, single-pass
A collection noting that 1873 rests on Illing's The Art of Japanese Prints and that 1878 and 1879 are also given

rights: Met records and images CC0; makers' labels, coding and derived data CC BY 4.0 (house line).
seed: Object draw seeded (random.Random(20261118 + department id)); the face's draw is made in the reader's browser; makers are model instances and not seeded
